key_insight: Most adults starting metformin alone had a sustained HbA1c improvement, but a small subgroup showed poor glycemic response.
clinical_relevance: Routine HbA1c monitoring within the first 6 months after metformin initiation may help identify patients who are not responding as expected.
method: Observational cohort of 140,413 U.S. Veterans Affairs patients starting metformin monotherapy
Latent class mixed models identified HbA1c trajectory patterns over 2 years
Random forests were used to predict trajectory class membership from routine clinical data
evidence_signal: The study analyzed 487,604 HbA1c measurements and found three trajectory groups, with model performance strong for brisk response prediction (91% accuracy) but weaker for non-response (59% accuracy).
watch_item: Because the cohort was drawn from the U.S. Veterans Affairs system, generalizability to broader populations and women may be limited.
paper_title: Glycemic response trajectories on metformin monotherapy in real-world diabetes care
